title: Section 2(1)(j) - Definition of Invention
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: In this Act, 'invention' means a new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application. For Ayurvedic and natural products, an invention must exhibit clear technical character and non-obviousness over existing classical texts.

title: Section 2(1)(ja) - Definition of Inventive Step
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: 'Inventive step' means a feature of an invention that involves technical advance as compared to the existing knowledge or having economic significance or both and that makes the invention not obvious to a person skilled in the art.

title: Section 3(a) - Frivolous and Immoral Inventions Exclusion
section_title: Section 3(a) - Frivolous and Immoral Inventions Exclusion
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: An invention which is frivolous or which claims anything obviously contrary to well established natural laws is not an invention within the meaning of this Act.

title: Section 3(b) - Inventions Contrary to Public Order or Morality
section_title: Section 3(b) - Inventions Contrary to Public Order or Morality
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: An invention the primary or intended use or commercial exploitation of which would be contrary to public order or morality or which causes serious prejudice to human, animal or plant life or health or to the environment.

title: Section 3(c) - Discovery of Scientific Principles or Living Things
section_title: Section 3(c) - Discovery of Scientific Principles or Living Things
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: The mere discovery of a scientific principle or the formulation of an abstract theory or discovery of any living thing or non-living substance occurring in nature is not an invention.

title: Section 3(d) - Incremental Innovations and Efficacy Requirement
section_title: Section 3(d) - Incremental Innovations and Efficacy Requirement
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant. In herbal formulations, extraction methods or new dosage delivery forms must establish significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy over the known herbal raw substance.

title: Section 3(e) - Mere Admixture Exclusion
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance is not patentable. Polyherbal formulations must prove unexpected synergistic interaction (e.g. Combination Index < 1.0) rather than simple addition of known herbal bioactives.

title: Section 3(f) - Arrangement or Duplication of Known Devices
section_title: Section 3(f) - Arrangement or Duplication of Known Devices
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: The mere arrangement or re-arrangement or duplication of known devices each functioning independently of one another in a known way.

title: Section 3(h) - Method of Agriculture or Horticulture
section_title: Section 3(h) - Method of Agriculture or Horticulture
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: A method of agriculture or horticulture cannot be patented in India. Standard methods of cultivating, harvesting, or organic farming of Ayurvedic medicinal plants are excluded.

title: Section 3(i) - Methods of Treatment and Diagnostic Methods
section_title: Section 3(i) - Methods of Treatment and Diagnostic Methods
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Any process for the medicinal, surgical, curative, prophylactic, diagnostic, therapeutic or other treatment of human beings or any similar treatment of animals to render them free of disease or to increase their economic value or that of their products is not patentable.

title: Section 3(j) - Plants, Animals and Biological Processes
section_title: Section 3(j) - Plants, Animals and Biological Processes
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Plants and animals in whole or any part thereof other than micro-organisms; but including seeds, varieties and species and essentially biological processes for production or propagation of plants and animals are excluded from patentability.

title: Section 3(k) - Computer Programs and Mathematical Methods
section_title: Section 3(k) - Computer Programs and Mathematical Methods
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: A mathematical or business method or a computer programme per se or algorithms are excluded from patentability.

title: Section 3(p) - Traditional Knowledge Exclusion
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: An invention which in effect is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components is not an invention within the meaning of this Act and cannot be patented in India. Merely combining known Ayurvedic herbs (such as Ashwagandha, Turmeric, or Tulsi) without demonstrating an unexpected synergistic technical effect beyond the sum of their individual known properties will result in statutory refusal under Section 3(p).

title: Section 8 - Information and Undertaking Regarding Foreign Applications
section_title: Section 8 - Information and Undertaking Regarding Foreign Applications
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: The applicant for a patent shall file along with his application a statement setting out detailed particulars of any applications for a patent for the same or substantially the same invention filed outside India.

title: Section 10(4) - Contents of Complete Specification
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Every complete specification shall fully and particularly describe the invention and its operation or use and the method by which it is to be performed; disclose the best method of performing the invention known to the applicant; and define the scope of the invention for which protection is claimed.

title: Section 10(4)(d)(ii) - Mandatory Disclosure of Biological Resource Origin
section_title: Section 10(4)(d)(ii) - Mandatory Disclosure of Biological Resource Origin
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Under Section 10(4)(d)(ii) of the Patents Act, 1970, every complete specification must disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material specified in the specification when used in an invention. If the biological resource is obtained from India, prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) under Section 6 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 must be obtained before the grant of the patent.

title: Section 10(5) - Unity of Invention and Single Inventive Concept
section_title: Section 10(5) - Unity of Invention and Single Inventive Concept
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: The claim or claims of a complete specification shall relate to a single invention, or to a group of inventions linked so as to form a single inventive concept, shall be clear and succinct and shall be fairly based on the matter disclosed in the specification.

title: Section 25(1)(k) - Opposition: Anticipation by Traditional Knowledge
section_title: Section 25(1)(k) - Opposition: Anticipation by Traditional Knowledge
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Any person may give notice of opposition to the Controller on the ground that the complete specification does not disclose or wrongly mentions the source or geographical origin of biological material used for the invention, or that the invention was anticipated having regard to knowledge, oral or otherwise, available within any local or indigenous community in India or elsewhere.

title: Section 25(2) - Post-Grant Patent Opposition Grounds
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: At any time after the grant of patent but before the expiry of a period of one year from the date of publication of grant of a patent, any person interested may give notice of opposition to the Controller on statutory grounds including non-patentability under Section 3(p) or non-disclosure of biological source under Section 10(4)(d)(ii).

title: Section 39 - Residents not to apply for Patents outside India without Prior Permission
section_title: Section 39 - Residents not to apply for Patents outside India without Prior Permission
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: No person resident in India shall, except under the authority of a written permit granted by the Controller, make or cause to be made any application outside India for the grant of a patent for an invention unless an application for a patent for the same invention has been made in India not less than six weeks before the application outside India.

title: Section 48 - Rights of Patentee
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: A patent granted under this Act shall confer upon the patentee the exclusive right to prevent third parties, who do not have his consent, from the act of making, using, offering for sale, selling or importing for those purposes that product in India.

title: Section 54 - Patents of Addition
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Where an application is made for a patent in respect of any improvement in or modification of an invention described or disclosed in the complete specification, the applicant may request that the patent for the improvement be granted as a patent of addition.

title: Section 84 - Compulsory Licensing Grounds
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: At any time after the expiration of three years from the date of the grant of a patent, any person interested may make an application to the Controller for grant of compulsory licence on grounds that reasonable requirements of the public have not been satisfied or the patented invention is not available at a reasonably affordable price.

title: Section 107A - Bolar Exemption and Parallel Importation
section_title: Section 107A - Bolar Exemption and Parallel Importation
authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Any act of making, constructing, using, selling or importing a patented invention solely for uses reasonably related to the development and submission of information required under any law for the time being in force, in India, or in a country other than India, that regulates the manufacture, construction, use or sale of any product, shall not be considered as an infringement of patent rights.

authority: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
publisher: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
content: Statutory provision under Section 6 of the Indian Patents Act, 1970 governing procedural requirements, Controller powers, examination, registers, revocation, appellate board proceedings, and statutory compliance for IP rights in India.
